1176278285950554112.a: We had this happen with SWISH-E back in the early 2000s when it was common practice to steal Open Source and Free Software and pretend like you wrote it. Multiple instances of companies embedding our code in proprietary apps without obeying our license and copyright.

1176278861027430400.a: Stealing code, even if it is simply a case of scrubbing copyright info, and then making it part of an Open Source project? Reprehensibly unforgivable. Unless you rewrote all the code to implement the same API you don't get to do that. And the law tends to agree, aggressively.

1176279768653795330.a: And I will note... We also did that with SWISH-E. We came to a point that most of the old HP code was simply gone. We took a moment to ensure we had scrubbed all HP code and changed licenses accordingly. It was disingenuous to keep giving HP rights to code they didn't write, IMHO
